steps.content: Every murky shadow tells a tragic end.
The malice from the Abyss, the true culprit of the tragedy, the truth you've long suspected but dared not—would not—confront... It's enough. You've seen more than enough.
But you will go on. You must go on.
Blinding white light floods your vision. You find yourself on an unfamiliar, clear azure sea.
Spacing out?
A white shadow extends a hand. Unlike the murky shadows you met before, this one is hollow. A puppet performing scripted scenes regardless of your response.
I know this is your first time at sea. It's natural to feel a little scared.
But don't worry. We have the wisest scholars with us, the bravest captain and sailors on these seas.
The torch of human civilization is in our hands... We'll solve the mystery of the disaster and bring a future full of hope.
[Scene Change]
In the biting winds, civilization and humanity—love and hope—proved so fragile.
"Future" became a joke. In the brutal present, survival was the only problem to solve.
It was a blizzard no one saw coming. No scholar could explain how, at summer's end, the research vessel became trapped by sea ice. Everyone was stranded.
Four long months passed. No rescue, not even a word from the outside world. Supplies long exhausted, hunger turned the finest of humanity into the most primitive of beasts.
The same hands meant to hold "the torch of human civilization" were now covered in fine bite marks.
This is a necessary sacrifice.
They spoke these words while slurping the last drops of marrow from finger bones.
...He's already dead. There's nothing we can do to change that.
Be rational, my child. We have... no other choice.
[Scene transition, a mental space]
She was the most rational of them all.
She had a deceptively gentle façade and the foresight to see things through. Patiently, she waited as bloodthirsty instincts consumed every soul less rational than she was.
She witnessed the entirety of the bloody feast, yet remained true only to herself. And thus, effortlessly, she survived to the end.
Then, she beheld the final prize.
From the desperate madness of her former companions, upon their corpses bereft of sanity or reason, a strange new life was born, glimmering with a radiance entirely alien to humankind.
That was the Apostle they spoke of—and the one true goal of their voyage.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: It is a species far more beautiful than humanity.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: It accepted everything, absorbed everything. Empty ideals, pretentious virtues, or the most primitive fear and despair... It embraced them all.
You don't know when the pale gray figure you've been chasing appeared silently by your side.
Shin, the expedition's oceanographer, the woman synonymous with compassion, understanding, leadership... all those positive words.
Now that you see her again, she's no different from when you first met her. Calm, patient, confident, like the perfect mother one could only find in a storybook.
But you know she's nothing like the woman you met on the ship. You take a wary step back.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Was this your true purpose all along? Did you... KILL them?

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: When I joined this expedition, I expected to see a repeat of the past, the same drama of betrayal and slaughter I remembered from before.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: But things were different this time.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Everyone on the crew... Dreya, Marguerite, Vanilla, Pylgia... even the two children who guided us on the way... everyone on the ship was so brave, strong, and rational.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Without their efforts, we never would have come so close to the truth. In them, I saw that humanity still carried a spark.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: And that's precisely why I find it so regrettable.
[Insert special effects + more intense BGM + Shin changes pose or form]

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: You had the courage to come this far, to stand before the greatest of truths, to witness a more powerful form of life and new possibilities for evolution. One more step, and you could transcend the narrow confines of human perception.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Why do you insist on covering your eyes and shackling your feet?

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Why cling so stubbornly to the concept of humanity? You embark on this journey, merely to understand the Perishing Star so you can fight it; so that humanity can endure to pit their feeble flesh against greater beings.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Why not cross that line? Why not abandon your weakness and become a grander form of life?
Even though you'd guessed the truth, hearing her say it aloud hits you with a nauseating chill so intense it's almost unreal.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You let the monsters into the ship...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You assigned everyone's tasks, pushing their minds to breaking points.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You drew its gaze to this ship. You misled me into searching for land that never existed.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Yes. It gazed upon this ship, and every soul aboard.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: It embraced them, welcomed them into its vastness... But they were ungrateful. They were terrified. They fought desperately to escape, even tried to harm it.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: A pity, but thankfully, things turned out as they should have. Except...

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Only I...
She covers her face, as if about to weep.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Every one of them was chosen. Every one of them earned its gaze.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Why am I the only one left behind?

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: I worked so hard to plan everything. I arranged every detail, just to reach it. But in the end, I'm the only one left behind, unable to reach the other side.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: What am I still missing?

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: You can give me the answer, can't you, my little guide?
You stare at her smile, fists clenched. She's still smiling, like always, like a gentle, patient mother.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Because you don't need my help. You don't need to abandon anything, or even endure physical death, to arrive at this place.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: I never misled you. It was your will that brought everyone here.
She crouches down and strokes your hair. Her soft touch and tender words, once so comforting, now stir your deepest fears.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: After all, <color=#fb9259>you came from the other side</color>.

steps.speaker: Shin
steps.content: Take me to it, my little guide. Only you know the way.
